week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers meet Johnny Appleseed as a kind tree planter through stories, seed play, orchard pretend, and simple life-cycle pictures. They touch large seeds or pom alternatives, plant pretend or supervised seeds, build trees with process art, and harvest pretend apples. Counting stays playful (touch and move) — not worksheets or accuracy drills. Life-cycle sequencing uses three large picture cards with adult support. The week is outdoor-friendly, short-turn, and kindness-focused.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice gentle planting care and kindness language with peers.
Language: Hear and try words such as seed, plant, grow, tree, water, orchard, and kind.
Cognitive: Explore seed-to-tree ideas with 3 picture cards and simple pretend sequences.
Fine motor: Scoop soil, stick collage pieces, and place large apples/seeds.
Gross motor: Dance watering motions, harvest carries, and parade marches.
Sensory: Explore soil/seed bins with safe fillers and gloves as needed.
Creative: Process tree crafts, orchard collages, and Johnny hats.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: whole apples (look), baskets, baskets for harvest, spray bottles/toy watering cans, blocks, baskets, smocks, towels
Science: apple halves (teacher-cut), large seeds or brown pom alternatives, 3 life-cycle picture cards, magnifiers
Sensory: soil or cocoa-cloud dough, scoops, cups; gloves optional
Art: brown/green paper, glue sticks, apple stickers, cotton “blossoms,” paint, craft sticks
Dramatic play: orchard trees (wall or standees), harvest baskets, helper badges
Literacy: Johnny Appleseed (Jodie Shepherd); The Seasons of Arnold's Apple Tree; Ten Red Apples; The Apple Pie Tree
Optional printables: 3-card life cycle set; orchard zone signs
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: teacher-cut apples for seed looking; sort large seeds or pom alternatives (avoid choking-size real seeds for mouthers).
Print/laminate 3 large life-cycle cards: seed → young tree → apple tree.
Prep soil bin and plant cups for Tuesday; decide real seed vs pretend plant plan.
Pre-cut tree trunks, crowns, and hat bands.
Choose 2–3 books; place in reading basket.
Allergy check if any apple tasting is offered during the week (optional only).
prepChecklist: Prepare large seeds or pom alternatives
Teacher-cut apple halves for discovery (no child knives)
Prep soil sensory bin + gloves option
Pre-cut tree craft and hat pieces
Allergy plan if any optional tasting
week.observationFocus:
Curiosity with seeds/soil
Kindness and gentle hands
Playful counting/touching (not accuracy)
Interest in 3-card sequencing with support
Sensory preferences in garden bin
Engagement in orchard roles
week.familyConnection: Invite families to look for a tree on a walk and talk about what plants need (sun, water, care). Optional: plant a seed together at home—no required homework. Share that classroom “counting” is playful touching/moving, not worksheets.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry, gloves for soil, larger manipulatives, and adult-supported 3-card order. Never force tasting if apples are offered. Keep counting playful.

activities.title: Apple Seed Discovery
activities.objective: Discover that apples hold seeds by looking at teacher-cut apple halves and exploring large seed manipulatives.
activities.description: Toddlers look at teacher-cut apple halves, use magnifiers if interested, and touch large brown seeds or pom alternatives on a tray—no small choking seeds for mouthers.
activities.materials:
Apples cut in half (teacher-only knife work)
Large seed manipulatives or brown poms
Trays; magnifying glasses
Picture: apple with seeds
Wipes; handwashing
activities.preparation: Cut apples before children arrive. Sort seed alternatives by size. Allergy plan if any taste later.
activities.setup: Discovery tray for 2–3 toddlers with look-first samples.
activities.steps:
1. Show whole apple, then open half.
2. Point to seed pockets.
3. Invite touch of large seed alternatives.
4. Optional magnifier look.
5. Wash hands—seeds stay on tray.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where are the seeds?
Tiny seeds live inside.
Touch the big seed helpers.
Seeds can grow trees!
activities.observationOpportunities: Curiosity, pointing, willingness to touch, vocabulary for seed/apple.
activities.safetyNotes: Teacher-only cutting. Real apple seeds can be choking hazards—use large alternatives for independent touch. Wash hands. No forcing tastes.
activities.cleanupTips: Discard cut fruit per food policy; sanitize trays; store poms.
teacherTips: Keep real seeds in a closed look-jar if needed.

substitutions.use: Clear photo of apple cross-section + pom seeds

activities.adaptations: Look-only jars; gloves; watching first.
activities.extensions: Compare seed pom to a leaf or stick from the playground.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger look; older place seeds on apple picture.
observationPrompts: Did the child point to seeds?
Did they touch manipulatives?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Discovery tray with teacher-cut apple halves and large brown pom seeds, magnifiers nearby. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Johnny's Apple Tree
activities.objective: Build a process-art apple tree using trunk and crown pieces with open-ended sticking—no identical craft models.
activities.description: Toddlers glue a brown trunk and green crown shapes, then add apple stickers or dots anywhere they choose.
activities.materials:
Paper backgrounds
Pre-cut brown trunks and green crowns
Glue sticks
Apple stickers or red dabbers
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-cut shapes. Portion stickers. No sample-to-copy display.
activities.setup: Art table with shape trays.
activities.steps:
1. Name Johnny’s tree.
2. Glue trunk and crown freely.
3. Add apples anywhere.
4. Share trees at child height.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where does your trunk go?
Sticky tree!
Apples up high or down low?
Johnny planted trees with kindness.
activities.observationOpportunities: Glue use, placement choices, theme connection language.
activities.safetyNotes: Large stickers. Supervise glue. Non-toxic materials.
activities.adaptations: Pre-glued trunk; sticker-only apples; hand-under-hand.
activities.extensions: Add cotton blossom on some trees.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers on prepared tree; older assemble pieces.
observationPrompts: Did the child stick at least one piece independently?
Did they say tree/apple?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process-art apple trees with trunks, crowns, and stickers—varied child outcomes. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Count the Apple Seeds
activities.objective: Playfully touch and move large seed manipulatives while hearing number words—no worksheets or accuracy drills.
activities.description: Toddlers move large seeds/poms into a bowl or apple tray while the teacher models playful counting (one, two, more). Accuracy is not required.
activities.materials:
Large brown poms or jumbo seed counters
Bowls or apple ice-cube trays
Basket
Optional number song
activities.preparation: Remove small seeds. Set 5–6 counters per child max.
activities.setup: Small-group counting play rug or table.
activities.steps:
1. Show a handful of big seeds.
2. Touch-move into bowl together.
3. Teacher counts playfully; child joins if ready.
4. Dump and repeat.
5. All done—seeds rest in basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Touch one seed.
Move two seeds.
More seeds!
We can count by playing.
All done counting.
activities.observationOpportunities: One-to-one touch attempts, interest in number words, motor control moving counters.
activities.safetyNotes: Large counters only. Supervise mouthing. No worksheets, tracing, or drill practice.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Count-move pinecones as “seeds” outdoors if large enough.
teacherTips: Keep it playful—stop when interest drops.

substitutions.use: Large bottle caps or blocks as seeds

activities.adaptations: Fewer counters; hand-under-hand touch; watching peers count.
activities.extensions: Hide seeds in a bin for find-and-touch.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger dump/fill; older touch-count with teacher.
observationPrompts: Did the child touch-move counters?
Did they echo any number word?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddlers moving large pom seeds into bowls—playful, no worksheets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Growing Apple Trees
activities.objective: Act out seed-to-tree growth with body movements and a short growing chant.
activities.description: Toddlers curl as seeds, slowly stretch to standing trees, then “hold apples” with hands before swaying in the wind.
activities.materials:
Open space
LLH Growing Like a Tree Chant
Optional seed/tree picture cues
activities.preparation: Clear floor. Practice cues: seed / grow / tree / apples.
activities.setup: Scattered spots with room to stretch.
activities.steps:
1. Curl small like a seed.
2. Rain/water patter fingers.
3. Stretch up tall—tree!
4. Hands make apple shapes.
5. Sway and rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Tiny seed.
Water the seed.
Grow, grow, grow!
Tall apple tree!
Sway in the wind.
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation, body awareness, listening to movement cues.
activities.safetyNotes: Space out. Soft floor. No climbing on furniture as trees.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Grow like trees on the playground grass.
activities.adaptations: Lap support for balance; scarf “leaves” for arm movers.
activities.extensions: Let a child choose seed vs tree pose for the group.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce grow motions; toddlers stand.
observationPrompts: Did the child try curl and stretch?
Did they follow a cue?

activities.title: Plant Your Own Apple Seed
activities.objective: Practice a toddler planting sequence—scoop soil, place a large seed/pom, and water with a gentle spray—without expecting real germination success.
activities.description: Each toddler fills a cup with soil, plants a large seed alternative (or real seed with tight supervision), and mists with a spray bottle. Emphasize care and kindness, not science fair results. Pretend planting is fully valid.
activities.materials:
Clear cups or pots
Potting soil or clean sensory soil alternative
Large seed/pom OR real seed (supervised)
Spray bottles / toy cans with little water
Trays; smocks; gloves optional
Picture steps: scoop → plant → water
activities.preparation: Allergy/soil sensitivity check. Pre-moisten soil slightly. Decide real vs pretend seeds. Cover floor.
activities.setup: Planting station for 2 toddlers at a time with picture steps.
activities.steps:
1. Scoop soil into cup.
2. Make a finger hole.
3. Place seed/pom.
4. Cover gently.
5. Mist water—kind care.
6. Place cups on a “garden window” tray.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Scoop the soil.
Seed in the hole.
Cover, cover.
Gentle water.
We care like Johnny.
activities.observationOpportunities: Sequencing with pictures, tool use, gentle hands, sensory response to soil.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise soil (no eating). Large seed alternatives preferred for mouthers. Minimal water to avoid slips. Wash hands after.
activities.cleanupTips: Sweep soil; wipe trays; store spray bottles.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use cocoa cloud-dough “soil” if potting soil is too messy.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Plant in outdoor sensory table or garden bed edge with teacher.
teacherTips: Replace thin “plant and wait” lessons with care-sequence play.

substitutions.use: Crumbled cereal soil (allergy check) or brown play dough plant cups

activities.adaptations: Pre-filled cups for poke-and-plant only; gloves; watching first.
activities.extensions: Draw a sun paper to place beside cups.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger drop seed in pre-holed cup; older scoop soil.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt 2+ planting steps?
Did they use gentle water?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler planting cups with soil, large seeds, spray bottles, and picture steps. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.decisionNote: Replace thin plant-and-wait activity with toddler-safe care-sequence planting (large seeds/poms, pretend OK)

activities.title: Garden Sensory Bin
activities.objective: Explore garden textures—soil, scoops, and “seeds”—through open sensory play.
activities.description: Toddlers dig, scoop, and hide large seed poms in a shallow garden bin with scoops and cups.
activities.materials:
Shallow bin
Soil OR kinetic sand OR shredded brown paper
Scoops; cups; rakes
Large seed poms
Smocks; gloves optional
activities.preparation: Allergy check. Choose dry filler if wet soil is challenging. Remove small items.
activities.setup: Sensory table for 3 children with floor mat.
activities.steps:
1. Dig and scoop freely.
2. Hide and find seeds.
3. Fill cups like planters.
4. Wash hands when done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Dig, dig.
Find a seed!
Scoop into the pot.
How does the soil feel?
activities.observationOpportunities: Texture tolerance, scooping, persistence, peer space sharing.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise mouthing. No small seeds. Wash hands. Floor dry for footing.
activities.adaptations: Tools-only exploration; smaller personal tray; seated support.
activities.extensions: Add toy watering can for pretend water (empty indoors).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants sealed sensory bag; toddlers open bin.
observationPrompts: Did the child dig/scoop?
Any avoidance that needs alternative?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Shallow garden sensory bin with scoops, cups, and large seed poms. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Seed to Tree Craft
activities.objective: Create a simple process collage showing a seed and a tree side by side without worksheet sequencing.
activities.description: Toddlers glue a “seed” (pom/paper) on one side of paper and build a tree on the other with scraps—open-ended process art.
activities.materials:
Paper
Brown poms or paper seeds
Green/brown scraps
Glue sticks; stickers
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-fold paper in half lightly as optional guide—not labeled worksheet.
activities.setup: Art trays with seed and tree materials.
activities.steps:
1. Glue a seed on the page.
2. Build a tree with scraps.
3. Talk: seed grows into tree.
4. Display.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Here’s your seed.
Here’s your tree.
Seed to tree!
You made it your way.
activities.observationOpportunities: Glue control, understanding of two images with support, creative choices.
activities.safetyNotes: Large poms. Non-toxic glue. No small beans.
teacherTips: Do not require correct left-to-right order.
activities.adaptations: One side only; sticker trees; adult holds paper.
activities.extensions: Add a water drop sticker near the seed.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers; older multi-scrap trees.
observationPrompts: Did the child place both a seed and tree piece?
Did they echo grow/tree?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process seed-to-tree collages with varied child results. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Water the Garden Dance
activities.objective: Practice watering motions and freeze/grow cues through a garden dance.
activities.description: Toddlers pretend to water plants with arm motions or empty watering cans, then freeze as growing trees.
activities.materials:
Optional toy watering cans (empty)
Music/chant
Open space
Plant picture cards
activities.preparation: Clear space. Empty cans only indoors.
activities.setup: Scattered spots; cans available.
activities.steps:
1. Water low plants—bend gently.
2. Water tall trees—reach high.
3. Freeze and grow.
4. Twirl like sprinklers.
5. Rest cans.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Water, water.
Gentle rain.
Grow tall!
Freeze trees.
Garden helpers!
activities.observationOpportunities: Level changes, freeze listening, imaginative watering.
activities.safetyNotes: Empty cans indoors. No running. Watch slips if any real water outdoors.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Real tiny water on sidewalk plants if safe and permitted.
teacherTips: Keep motions gentle to match plant care.
activities.adaptations: Seated watering arms; partner help carrying can.
activities.extensions: Child leads water high/low.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants finger rain on laps; toddlers dance.
observationPrompts: Did the child water high and low?
Did they freeze?

activities.title: Apple Tree Life Cycle Sequencing
activities.objective: Order three large picture cards—seed, young tree, apple tree—with adult support; not a preschool worksheet.
activities.description: In a tiny group, toddlers look at three large life-cycle cards and place them in order with teacher modeling and hands-on help. Playful retell, not testing.
activities.materials:
3 large laminated cards: seed / young tree / apple tree
Floor mat or pocket chart at toddler height
Optional matching objects (pom, twig, plastic apple)
activities.preparation: Print large simple images. Avoid text-heavy charts. Practice a 3-sentence story.
activities.setup: Small-group circle with cards face up first (match) then order.
activities.steps:
1. Name each card together.
2. Match objects to cards if using.
3. Teacher models order: seed → young tree → apples.
4. Invite child to move cards with support.
5. Retell once; celebrate any attempt.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What comes first?
Seed in the ground.
Then a little tree.
Then apples!
You can move the cards—I’ll help.
activities.observationOpportunities: Attention to pictures, willingness to move cards, benefit from support, language for first/next.
activities.safetyNotes: Laminate edges smooth. No worksheets, cutting sequencing strips, or accuracy grading.
activities.cleanupTips: Store cards in a labeled envelope for Friday review.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Clip cards to a fence for outdoor order play.

substitutions.use: Three photos taken of classroom props

activities.adaptations: Two cards only; hand-over-hand placement; match without ordering.
activities.extensions: Act the three stages with bodies after cards.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers try alone first; younger match objects only.
observationPrompts: Did the child move a card with support?
Did they use seed/tree/apple words?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Three large life-cycle picture cards on a toddler mat with a teacher hand supporting ordering. No worksheets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Build an Apple Tree
activities.objective: Construct a 3D or textured process tree using tubes, paper, and stickers.
activities.description: Toddlers tape/glue green paper or tissue onto a cardboard tube trunk and add apple stickers for a standing process tree.
activities.materials:
Cardboard tubes
Green tissue/paper
Tape/glue
Apple stickers
Tray bases (paper plates)
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-attach tubes to plate bases for stability. Pre-tear tissue.
activities.setup: Build table with one trunk per child.
activities.steps:
1. Show standing trunk.
2. Stick on leaves freely.
3. Add apples.
4. Stand trees in a classroom “orchard row.”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Build your tree.
Leaves on top.
Apples here?
Our orchard is growing!
activities.observationOpportunities: Bilateral taping/gluing, vertical building interest, pride in orchard display.
activities.safetyNotes: Tape pieces pre-torn. Supervise mouthing of stickers. Stable bases to prevent tip injuries.
activities.cleanupTips: Stand trees to dry; wipe sticky tables.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Build trees outdoors; use natural leaf bits if safe.
activities.adaptations: Pre-leafed trunks for apple-sticker finish; seated support.
activities.extensions: Add cotton blossoms to some trees.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers on flat tree; older 3D build.
observationPrompts: Did the child add leaves or apples?
Did they help place tree in orchard row?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Standing process apple trees made from tubes and tissue in a classroom orchard row. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Count the Apples on the Tree
activities.objective: Playfully touch and move apple props on a tree display—number words without drill worksheets.
activities.description: Toddlers stick large apple cutouts or poms onto a wall tree and touch-count with the teacher in a playful way.
activities.materials:
Wall or easel tree outline
Large apple cutouts / red poms with sticky dots or Velcro
Basket
Optional chant
activities.preparation: Place tree at toddler height. Prep 6–8 apples max.
activities.setup: Standing tree station for 2–3 children.
activities.steps:
1. Put apples on the tree.
2. Touch each apple while teacher counts playfully.
3. Take some apples to a basket (harvest).
4. Put them back and repeat.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Put an apple on the tree.
Touch, touch—one, two.
More apples!
Harvest into the basket.
activities.observationOpportunities: Placing/removing, touch-counting attempts, turn-taking at the tree.
activities.safetyNotes: Large apples only. Secure tree display. No worksheets or required accurate totals.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect apples in basket; leave tree up for Thursday harvest.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Hang apples on a playground fence tree drawing.

substitutions.use: Felt tree board on a table

activities.adaptations: Fewer apples; adult holds child to reach; sitting felt board.
activities.extensions: Sort red vs green apples playfully.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stick on; older touch-count with teacher.
observationPrompts: Did the child place an apple?
Did they join touch-counting?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler-height tree display with large removable apple props—no worksheets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Growing Through the Seasons
activities.objective: Move through simple seasonal actions connected to an apple tree story.
activities.description: Toddlers act spring blossoms, summer leaves, fall harvest reaches, and winter still trees using short cues—no long calendar lesson.
activities.materials:
Season picture cards (4 simple images)
Open space
Optional scarves
Book tie-in: The Seasons of Arnold's Apple Tree (short picture walk)
activities.preparation: Choose 4 clear season cues. Keep language concrete.
activities.setup: Circle or scatter spots with cards visible.
activities.steps:
1. Spring—flutter blossom fingers.
2. Summer—stretch leaf arms.
3. Fall—reach and pick apples.
4. Winter—still freeze tree.
5. Repeat once and rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Spring blossoms!
Summer leaves stretch.
Fall—pick apples!
Winter still trees.
Seasons change.
activities.observationOpportunities: Cue response, seasonal word exposure, movement variety.
activities.safetyNotes: Clear space. Soft freeze holds. Keep lesson short—exposure, not mastery of seasons.
teacherTips: Picture cards matter more than month names.
Pair with a brief book picture walk earlier.

substitutions.use: Weather icons: rain, sun, wind, snow

activities.adaptations: Seated motions; fewer seasons (fall/winter only).
activities.extensions: Child picks next season card.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants scarf flutter; toddlers full sequence.
observationPrompts: Did the child try two season motions?
Did they notice a picture cue?

activities.title: Harvest the Apples
activities.objective: Pretend to work in an apple orchard—pick, carry, and sort apples with simple helper roles.
activities.description: Toddlers pick plastic/fabric apples from a low tree or basket tree, carry them in harvest baskets, and sort into color bowls.
activities.materials:
Low tree prop or wall apples
Plastic/fabric apples (large)
Harvest baskets
Color bowls (red/green)
Helper badges
Optional wagon
activities.preparation: Stage orchard zone. Limit apples to prevent clutter. Sanitize props.
activities.setup: Tree → path → sort table.
activities.steps:
1. Put on helper badges.
2. Pick apples gently.
3. Carry basket to table.
4. Sort by color if interested.
5. Rest apples for market.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Orchard helpers ready?
Pick gently.
Carry your basket.
Red or green?
Great harvesting!
activities.observationOpportunities: Role play, carrying control, sorting interest, cooperative space use.
activities.safetyNotes: Large apples only. Walking feet. No climbing furniture to “reach trees.”
activities.cleanupTips: Return apples to tree/bin; stack baskets.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Outdoor orchard harvest walk with hidden apples.
teacherTips: Two roles max: picker and sorter.
activities.adaptations: Shorter path; pre-filled baskets to sort only; wagon push option.
activities.extensions: Open a pretend farm stand after harvest.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger pick into shared basket; older sort colors.
observationPrompts: Did the child pick and carry?
Did they attempt sorting?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler orchard dramatic play with baskets and large apple props at a low tree. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Healthy Apple Trees
activities.objective: Explore what trees need to stay healthy—sun, water, and gentle care—through object sorting and pretend care.
activities.description: Toddlers sort picture/object cards into “helps the tree” vs “not for trees” with teacher support, then pretend to water and give sunshine.
activities.materials:
Tree prop
Cards/objects: sun, water can, soil, snack wrapper, toy car (not for tree)
Two trays: Helps / Not now
Spray bottle (empty or mist)
activities.preparation: Prepare clear photo cards. Keep sort playful, not test-like.
activities.setup: Small-group discovery with tree in center.
activities.steps:
1. Show healthy tree.
2. Sort one helper item together.
3. Children place cards on trays with support.
4. Water and “shine” the tree.
5. Kind words for the tree.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What helps our tree?
Sun helps!
Water helps.
Cars? Not for trees.
We take care.
activities.observationOpportunities: Sorting with support, care actions, vocabulary for sun/water/care.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep it simple—two categories. No shame for “wrong” sorts; model calmly.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Real tree visit: talk about sun/water outdoors.
teacherTips: Focus on care habits, not botany lectures.
activities.adaptations: One helper item to place; adult narrates; match identical pictures.
activities.extensions: Add a kindness card: share apples.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger bring water can to tree; older sort several cards.
observationPrompts: Did the child place an item with support?
Did they water or shine?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Tree prop with Helps/Not now trays and sun/water cards. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Apple Orchard Collage
activities.objective: Create an open-ended orchard collage with paper, stickers, and scraps—process art as the proposed cover activity.
activities.description: Toddlers fill a large paper with trees, apples, and sky pieces using glue and stickers. No identical models; process only.
activities.materials:
Large paper
Green/brown/red scraps
Glue sticks
Apple stickers
Cotton clouds optional
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-tear scraps. Cover tables. Plan photo of setup for cover later.
activities.setup: Collage table with shared scrap trays.
activities.steps:
1. Name “orchard.”
2. Glue freely—trees, apples, sky.
3. Add stickers.
4. Title child’s work with their name.
5. Display orchard gallery.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What will grow in your orchard?
Glue a tree.
Apples everywhere!
Your orchard is unique.
activities.observationOpportunities: Creative covering, fine-motor sticking, theme vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Large scraps. Non-toxic glue. Process art—no craft perfection pressure.
teacherTips: Primary cover candidate—capture realistic setup photo later.
activities.adaptations: Sticker-only orchard; smaller paper; tray boundaries.
activities.extensions: Add a Johnny helper sticker walking in the orchard.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers; older multi-layer scraps.
observationPrompts: Did the child fill space with materials?
Did they use orchard/tree words?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic toddler orchard collage in progress with scraps and stickers—cover candidate. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Orchard Workers Song
activities.objective: Sing and move as orchard workers—pick, carry, and stack—to build rhythm and role language.
activities.description: Toddlers perform simple orchard job motions during a short song/chant, then freeze for a water break pose.
activities.materials:
Music player or teacher chant
Optional baskets
Open space
activities.preparation: Choose 3 motions: pick, carry, stack.
activities.setup: Circle with baskets available.
activities.steps:
1. Pick apples—reach.
2. Carry baskets—march.
3. Stack apples—place.
4. Wipe brow—break.
5. Cheer orchard workers.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Pick, pick.
Carry, carry.
Stack the apples.
Orchard workers help!
Hooray!
activities.observationOpportunities: Motion imitation, group rhythm, role pride.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking marches only. Lightweight baskets.
teacherTips: Use baskets only if they don’t cause collisions.
activities.adaptations: Seated pick/stack; partner carry.
activities.extensions: Child chooses next orchard job.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce pick motions; toddlers move.
observationPrompts: Did the child try pick and carry?
Did they enjoy group song?

activities.title: Apple Tree Life Cycle Review
activities.objective: Review the three life-cycle cards and act each stage briefly to close the science thread.
activities.description: Toddlers revisit seed / young tree / apple tree cards, order with support, and do a quick body retell.
activities.materials:
Same 3 large life-cycle cards
Optional objects: pom, twig, apple
Mat
activities.preparation: Have cards ready from Wednesday.
activities.setup: Small-group review circle.
activities.steps:
1. Show cards out of order.
2. Order with support.
3. Act seed → grow → apples.
4. Cheer “We know the apple tree story!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
What comes first?
Seed… tree… apples!
Can your body be a seed?
Grow!
Apples!
activities.observationOpportunities: Recall with support, enjoyment of retell, reduced prompting needs vs Wednesday.
activities.safetyNotes: Support expected. No quiz grades. Keep joyful.
activities.cleanupTips: Store cards for future apple weeks.
teacherTips: Compare to Wednesday only for teacher notes—not child pressure.
activities.adaptations: Match objects to cards without ordering; adult orders while child acts.
activities.extensions: Invite a stuffed animal to “watch” the retell.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger act only; older move cards.
observationPrompts: Did the child need less help than before?
Did they join the body retell?

activities.title: Johnny Appleseed Hat
activities.objective: Decorate a simple process-art pot-style or band hat inspired by Johnny’s story for parade wear.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate paper pot hats or headbands with stickers and stamps—process art for pretend play, not historical costume accuracy.
activities.materials:
Paper pot hats or bands
Stickers; stampers; crayons
Apple cutouts
Tape to fit
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-form hats. Soften historical story to kindness + planting for toddlers.
activities.setup: Art table with hats and open materials.
activities.steps:
1. Try a plain hat—say Johnny helper.
2. Decorate freely.
3. Fit loosely.
4. Wear for parade.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Johnny helper hat!
Stickers anywhere.
You plant kindness.
Ready for the parade?
activities.observationOpportunities: Decorating choices, interest in role identity, fine motor sticking.
activities.safetyNotes: Loose fit; no covering eyes; no tight strings. Large stickers.
activities.cleanupTips: Store hats for parade same day.
teacherTips: Keep Johnny story toddler-simple: kind planter.
activities.adaptations: Pre-decorated band + one sticker choice; apron alternative.
activities.extensions: Add a seed packet sticker “for planting.”
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger sticker band; older pot hat collage.
observationPrompts: Did the child engage in decorating?
Did the hat lead to pretend planting?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process-decorated Johnny helper hats on a table with stickers and stampers. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Apple Orchard Counting Challenge
activities.objective: Celebrate playful orchard counting by moving apples along a challenge path—touch and carry, not worksheet drills.
activities.description: Toddlers complete a playful “challenge”: gather a small handful of apples, touch-count with a teacher, and deliver to a basket finish. Accuracy not required.
activities.materials:
Large apple props
Start basket and finish basket
Short path markers
Optional badges
activities.preparation: Set a short clear path. Limit to a few apples.
activities.setup: Challenge path with start/finish.
activities.steps:
1. Pick 1–3 apples (child choice).
2. Touch-count together playfully.
3. Carry to finish basket.
4. Sticker/high-five.
5. Repeat if interested.
activities.teacherLanguage:
How many will you carry?
Touch each apple.
One, two… more!
To the orchard basket!
You did the challenge!
activities.observationOpportunities: Choice-making, touch-count participation, path completion, pride.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet. Large props. No worksheets, timers, or accuracy scoring. Keep pressure low—challenge = playful invitation.
teacherTips: Rename “challenge” as adventure if competition arises.
activities.adaptations: Carry one apple only; wagon delivery; adult counts while child touches.
activities.extensions: Sort delivered apples into two finish baskets.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger carry one; older choose a handful to touch-count.
observationPrompts: Did the child complete a delivery?
Did they touch-count with support?

activities.title: Johnny Appleseed Parade
activities.objective: Close the week with a kindness parade celebrating planting helpers and orchard play.
activities.description: Toddlers wear hats, carry a seed pouch or apple prop, and parade while chanting a short kindness/planting line, then group cheer.
activities.materials:
Johnny hats
Seed pouches (paper bags) or apple props
Parade path
Chant/song
Optional stickers
activities.preparation: Clear loop. Stage props. Keep Johnny message: kind planter.
activities.setup: Line-up spots; music ready.
activities.steps:
1. Choose prop.
2. Parade two loops max.
3. Freeze and show prop.
4. Say “We plant kindness!”
5. Stickers and cheer.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Johnny helpers march!
What are you carrying?
Seeds or apples?
We plant kindness!
Hooray!
activities.observationOpportunities: Group participation, pride, recall of week props, comfort in parade.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet. Loose hats. No forced speaking. Large props.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect hats/props; store for next year.
activities.adaptations: Wagon parade; nonverbal prop show; adult partner.
activities.extensions: Family photo if permitted; send home kindness planting note.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants wave; toddlers parade.
observationPrompts: Did the child join the parade?
Did they show a prop or phrase with support?
